products.name: You.com Enterprise
products.note: Private search AI; no tracking; enterprise deployment; data privacy focus

reading.body:
You.com is a search-augmented LLM that lets AI systems query the web and ground their outputs in current information, addressing a core constraint on LLM deployment in production.

Search-grounded AI is infrastructure, not a consumer feature. You.com's split between a public search LLM and an enterprise product with data privacy controls reflects a real divergence in how AI applications need to operate. The startup was founded in 2020, which places it in the wave of companies built after large language models proved useful but before most enterprises had solved the problem of letting them access real-time information safely. For an AI system to answer questions about events, prices, or facts that change, it needs fresh data. A search API handles this without requiring the model itself to be retrained or the user to upload proprietary documents into a third-party LLM.

The enterprise variant is notable because it inverts the default assumption about AI infrastructure. Most search and data products assume tracking and resale of user behavior. You.com's enterprise offering explicitly markets the absence of tracking. This matters for companies deploying AI agents on sensitive tasks or proprietary data, where a search dependency creates a data leakage risk. The product design suggests the company has identified deployment as the constraint, not the technology.

The data does not specify You.com's compute footprint, power draw, or data center location. It does not indicate whether the company operates its own infrastructure or relies on cloud providers. The 174 California legal cases are recorded without context, so their relevance to the product line is unknown.

profile_text.body:
You.com is a for-profit startup founded in 2020 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company describes itself as offering web search APIs designed for AI applications, with a focus on enabling agents and large language models to search the web, extract clean content, and generate grounded answers.

The company tracks two main products. The first is You.com itself, a search-augmented LLM available at the main website. The second is You.com Enterprise, described as a private search AI product aimed at business deployment, with an emphasis on data privacy and no user tracking. The site characterizes its offerings as providing accuracy, freshness, and low latency suited to next-generation AI agents.

The held facts note a significant California legal exposure, with 174 cases associated with that jurisdiction, though no specific litigation details are recorded. No MCP server presence or SEC and patent filings are on file for the company.
